newsitem.title: USA: General Motors, UAW continue talks past deadline.
newsitem.headline: General Motors, UAW continue talks past deadline.

text.p: General Motors Corp said that contract negotiations with the United Auto Workers union were continuing past a midnight Sunday (0500 GMT) strike deadline without a walkout by workers.
A GM spokesman declined to provide further details of the talks, saying the automaker would make a more detailed statement later Monday.
"They're still on the job," said Norman Harp, a union commiteeman for UAW Local 14 at GM's Toledo, Ohio, transmission plant, which recently started its third shift.
"The deadline's here and gone and they're still talking," Harp added.

The UAW cancelled its national contract covering 215,000 GM hourly workers at 11:59 p.m. EST Sunday (0459 GMT Monday) in an effort to increase pressure on GM. Union officials say the two sides have been working to resolve differences over the union's demand that GM follow the pattern set at Ford Motor Co and Chrysler Corp by guaranteeing employment for 95 percent of its UAW workers.
GM wants to exclude several parts plants from the guarantees, including a door hardware plant in Flint, Mich., and an interior trim plant in Livonia, Mich., that it wants to sell.
